attributes.residual:
TWO REFUTATIONS AND ONE DESIGN REVERSAL, all reported rather than worked around.

(a) ITEM 5, HALF-REFUTED. `--revert restored the EDITED state` REPRODUCES verbatim: at a5215d1d3 on zlib/adler32, a clean BASELINE probe banked the pristine tree, a comment edit probed NEUTRAL (which banks by design), and `probe.py zlib/adler32 adler32 --revert` printed `nothing to restore: adler32's banked snapshot IS the current working tree` and left the edit in place. `re-banked the edited tree as BASELINE anyway - overwriting the clean revert point` does NOT: `baseline_bank_decision` keeps the session baseline once it exists and REFUSES to create a first one over an edited tree (run-48 item 5), so the .base was never overwritten in the reproduction. What was live is that the restore path re-scored THROUGH the banking block, which is what the fix removes.

(b) ITEM 8, HALF-REFUTED. `Select-String is case-insensitive by default` CONFIRMED (4 rows matched vs 3 with -CaseSensitive on a four-line array; this lane hit it live on its own first gate run). `Select-String on a long python stream corrupts the exit code the same way` REFUTED: measured on a 241-line stream, plain, `-List` and `-Quiet` forms ALL exit 0, and the corruption appears only with a `Select-Object -First` downstream (exit -1). Trap 6a's scope is unchanged.

(c) ITEM 1, DESIGN REVERSED by its own calibration, as above: no prose detector ships and the separation is recorded by the author as a field.
